description: Synthetic reference cases for the video playback and bar-path overlay design contract (docs/validation/VIDEO_OVERLAY_CONTRACT.md): display transform, timeline binding and frame lookup, path runs, and rep navigation. Expectations are hand-derived engineering references, not produced by an OpenBar implementation and not accuracy evidence.

transform_cases.description: 1920x1080 analysis drawn into a 960x540 view: scale 0.5, no bars. The frame corners are geometry probes (the outer edges of the first and last pixel), not valid observations.
Landscape analysis in a 1080x2400 portrait view: width-limited scale 0.5625, bars above and below.
Portrait analysis in a 1920x1080 landscape view: height-limited scale 0.5625, bars left and right.
720x1280 coded portrait recording with no rotation metadata, 360x640 view: scale 0.5.
1280x720 coded raster with source_rotation_deg 90: S1 is 720x1280. Coded pixels map through (cy, Wc-1-cx).
1280x720 coded raster with source_rotation_deg 180: S1 stays 1280x720, 640x360 view. Coded pixels map through (Wc-1-cx, Hc-1-cy).
1280x720 coded raster with source_rotation_deg 270: S1 is 720x1280. Coded pixels map through (Hc-1-cy, cx).
The player decodes a 1080x1920 clip at 540x960. The scale comes from the analysis raster, so the overlay lands where it would on a full-size surface.
Player raster 959x540 for a 1920x1080 analysis: both raster differences are at most 1 player pixel, so it is accepted.
Zoom 2 and pan (-100, 50) view pixels applied after the base transform: u' = Vw/2 + z*(u - Vw/2) + pan_x. The inverse undoes zoom and pan exactly.
Sample aspect ratio 4:3 is not supported (1:1 or unknown 0:1 only).
Player raster 1920x1088 (padded decoder surface) for a 1920x1080 analysis.
Dimensions match (720x1280) but the player reports it applied 270 degrees where the file says 90.
The Analysis has no identity.source_sha256, so it cannot be tied to the file being played. Everything else is valid; this is a refusal, not a pass.
The player cannot report the rotation it applied (null) and no conformance pass is recorded for the device class.
The player cannot report the rotation it applied, but a conformance pass is recorded for the device class: accepted.
Player raster 958x540 for a 1920x1080 analysis: the width differs from the proportional 960 by 2.

timeline_cases.description: Container start_pts 126000 at time base 1/90000 with frames every 3000 ticks. The player rebases to zero at the first frame, so its timestamps equal the canonical ones and the binding offset is 0.
Same stream, but the player keeps absolute presentation times offset by 1,400,000 us. The binding offset is 1,400,000 and every lookup resolves exactly as in the rebased case.

Phone-style clip: 1280x720 coded with source_rotation_deg 90 (display 720x1280), time base 1/90000, start_pts 126000, frame spacing 3000, 3300, 2700, 3600, 3000, 2400 ticks, and an absolute-PTS player (offset 1,400,000 us). Observations start at the seed frame 1 (frame 0 has none) and frame 3 is lost. The clock selects frames by floor; round(pos * 30) picks frame 2 where frame 1 is on screen at 69999 us.

Variable frame rate stream (time base 1/1000, frames at 0, 33, 75, 100, 141, 166 and 200 ms) whose metadata nominal_fps is 30. The playback clock selects the last frame at or before the position (floor); round(pos * nominal_fps) picks a different frame at 120000 us. naive_nominal_fps_index is informational only.

Ten-frame stream at 32 Hz with observations only for frames 3 to 6 (the analysed range). Frames outside it are not_analysed, including frames reached by the hold-last rule after the end of the stream.
Six-frame stream at 32 Hz where frame 2 is lost: the observation exists but has no coordinate, so the state is lost and no marker is drawn (not not_analysed). Neighbouring frames keep their markers.

A seek is requested at 85000 us, between the frames at 75000 us (frame 2) and 100000 us (frame 3). The player lands on the earlier keyframe, frame 1 (33000 us). While pending the marker is hidden (seeking); on completion the marker follows the presented frame 1, not the requested position.
Navigation to the sample at canonical t = 0.100 s (frame 3) needs a frame-exact seek. Success is reported only when the presented frame is the target; landing on frame 2 is seek_not_exact.
One frame's player timestamp is 2 ms away from its canonical time (a re-muxed copy or a moved edit list): the offsets disagree by 2000 us.
One offset differs by exactly 1 us, within the binding tolerance: accepted; the offset is the minimum (the first observation's offset is 1, the minimum 0).
One offset differs by 2 us, beyond the binding tolerance.
An observation without frame_index cannot be bound to a player frame.
Decoder provenance says probed_frame_count 10 but the player lists 9 frame timestamps, although every observation offset agrees.
An observation's frame_index (5) is beyond the player's frame list (5 frames, indices 0 to 4).
The adapter cannot list frame timestamps without decoding.

path_cases.description: Two lost observations in the middle end the first run; the next measured observation starts a new one. Nothing is drawn across the loss.
A low_confidence observation is a ring marker where tracked is filled, and every segment with a low_confidence endpoint is dashed.
A measured observation isolated by losses is a run of one, drawn as a dot; a following pair is a line.
Frame indices 10, 11, 13 are all tracked, but the missing frame 12 ends the run: consecutive observations are not consecutive frames.
A run never begins or ends at a lost observation: leading and trailing losses contribute nothing.

The emphasised trail is the same runs cut at the displayed observation index; the remainder is dimmed. Cuts at 0 and 4 (a run's first observation: emphasised is that single observation as a dot), 1 (inside a run), 3 (a lost observation: cuts the run before it, nothing emphasised at the loss), 5 (inside the second run) and 7 (the last observation).

navigation_cases.description: Three reps; the last follows a shorter preceding descent and is incomplete. All three are listed in order, each seeks to its metric interval start, and the incomplete one carries an incomplete flag.
A withheld rep with a long gap: listed with its reasons and no numbers, still seekable and highlighted over its window (the gap breaks the highlight at draw time).
A clip whose only positive-velocity run was rejected has no rep: the list is empty and the rejected run is not listed.

Observations lie on a 1/32 s grid. Rep 1 ends at 0.8046875 s and rep 2 starts at 0.953125 s, neither of which is an observation timestamp: the highlight is not drawn, nothing is snapped to the nearest frame, and the rep is flagged. A frame-exact seek needs a sample, so a start that is not an observation has no seek target.
